items.claim: VLAN hopping via switch spoofing or double-tagging lets an attacker escape a restricted VLAN and reach other segments.
items.body: Switch spoofing abuses DTP auto-trunking to make an access port become a trunk, granting access to all VLANs. Double-tagging nests an 802.1Q tag inside another to escape the native VLAN. Both are mitigated by disabling DTP, hardcoding access ports, and moving the native VLAN off VLAN 1.
items.disproof: DTP is disabled and ports are hardcoded as access, or VLAN hopping attempts are detected and blocked.

sources.quote: VLAN hopping via switch spoofing (abusing DTP auto-trunking) and double-tagging

items.claim: Classic perimeter firewalls only inspect north-south traffic, leaving east-west lateral movement largely unfiltered.
items.body: North-south flows cross the perimeter while east-west flows move between internal workloads. Perimeter firewalls see only the former, so lateral movement inside the network often goes unmonitored. Microsegmentation applies default-deny policy to east-west traffic to close this gap.
items.disproof: East-west traffic is inspected by internal firewalls or microsegmentation policy.

sources.quote: Classic perimeter firewalls only see north-south, leaving east-west largely unfiltered.
VLANs provide coarse macro-segmentation: all devices in a VLAN can still communicate freely with each other

items.claim: Attackers chain pivots through compromised hosts to reach segments that are not directly accessible from the initial foothold.
items.body: A compromised DMZ host may reach the internal LAN but not the database segment. The attacker pivots through the LAN host to reach the database segment, then onward to management VLANs. Network segmentation is effective only when no route exists between segments, forcing the attacker to compromise a new host in each segment.
items.disproof: No route exists between segments and firewall rules deny cross-segment traffic by default.

sources.quote: Initial compromise often provides access to only one network segment.
